     1	# Volume VIII — Recommendation Engine
     2	
     3	Status: Foundation aligned through Phase 6A
     4	Version: 2.1.0
     5	Last revised: 2026-07-20
     6	
     7	## 1. Purpose
     8	
     9	Define the research-recommendation subsystem: deterministic identity, candidate
    10	generation, persistence, duplicate handling, scoring/ranking, explicit human
    11	review, immutable advisory evidence, the explicitly separated manual conversion
    12	chain, read-only campaign planning/review, and explicit non-executing campaign
    13	approval, materialization, handoff observation, and exact materialized-proposal
    14	review.
    15	Phase 5 Step 1 adds an explicit atomic convenience that applies the existing
    16	Phase 4C paused conversion execution to every exact materialized campaign
    17	member, without activation, queueing, scheduler control, or workers.
    18	Phase 5 Step 2 adds the separately confirmed atomic convenience over existing
    19	Phase 4C activation, transitioning every exact eligible member from
    20	``paused/train`` to ``pending/train`` without starting scheduler or workers.
    21	Phase 5 Step 3 adds a distinct confirmed one-transaction launch convenience
    22	that composes those same execution and activation authorities for the exact
    23	membership without adding campaign state or scheduler behavior.
    24	Phase 5 Step 4 adds one deterministic read-only operational snapshot of every
    25	exact member's current Phase 4C, experiment, worker-metadata, inference, and
    26	analysis evidence without adding durable campaign state or scheduler behavior.
    27	Phase 5 Steps 5a–5b add a pure, non-authoritative scientific outcome assessment
    28	and its bounded, read-only authoritative-persisted-evidence integration. Step
    29	5c adds a separate pure, versioned advisory policy over that immutable
    30	assessment; it interprets but does not alter evidence, declare campaign
    31	success, or authorize follow-up.
    32	Phase 6A adds one pure immutable follow-up proposal bound to an exactly aligned
    33	eligible favorable Step 5C decision and its exact Step 5A assessment. The
    34	proposal is only an advisory candidate for later operator review and adds no
    35	persistence, approval, lifecycle, or scheduler authority.
    36	
    37	## 2. Scope
    38	
    39	### 2.1 In scope
    40	
    41	Recommendation policy and identities, pure candidates, scans, source evidence,
    42	duplicates, immutable scores/components, deterministic ranks/explanations,
    43	terminal review transitions, immutable review events, and deterministic
    44	evaluation classification/history, ranking snapshots and comparisons, plus the
    45	pure manually invoked proposed-experiment specification contract.
    46	The explicit Phase 4C manual conversion chain and Phase 4D campaign planning,
    47	review, explicit non-executing approval, and approved-campaign materialization
    48	into the existing Phase 4C proposal boundary, read-only handoff, and explicit
    49	campaign-wide Phase 4C proposal review are also in scope.
    50	The pure Phase 5 outcome contracts and the pure identity-bound Phase 6A
    51	follow-up proposal are in scope as non-persistent advisory values.
    52	
    53	### 2.2 Out of scope
    54	
    55	Automatic proposal creation, autonomous campaign execution or campaign
    56	management, profitability claims,
    57	recommendation-driven scheduler polling, worker execution, and automatic
    58	approval/rejection/expiration.
    59	
    60	### 2.3 Current implementation status
    61	
    62	Phase 4A Steps 1–5, Phase 4B Steps 1–2, Phase 4C Steps 1–6, Phase 4D Steps 1–6,
    63	Phase 5 Steps 1–5c, and Phase 6A implement the in-scope capabilities.
    64	Phase 4B Step 1 classifies current persisted provenance and reuses the Step 4
    65	score formula unchanged. Step 2 ranks only persisted Step 1 results, stores
    66	exact snapshot membership, and compares compatible persisted components.
    67	Phase 4C provides the explicit proposal, review, paused conversion, activation,
    68	and workflow-observation chain. Phase 4D Step 1 reads one explicit immutable
    69	ranking snapshot and Phase 4C workflow evidence to produce a deterministic,
    70	bounded campaign plan without persisting or executing it. Step 2 validates and
    71	reviews that plan with deterministic duplicates and coverage. Step 3 records
    72	one explicit immutable operator approval or rejection for an exactly
    73	reconstructed review without executing it. Step 4 atomically creates or reuses
    74	only that review's selected Phase 4C proposals; it does not review or execute
    75	them. Step 5 observes every exact materialized proposal, and Step 6 explicitly
    76	applies one ordinary Phase 4C review decision to all exact members atomically.
    77	Phase 5 Step 1 then permits a separately confirmed atomic execution of those
    78	exact members through the existing Phase 4C paused-conversion transaction
    79	primitive. It neither activates nor queues the created experiments.
    80	Phase 5 Step 2 separately applies the existing Phase 4C activation primitive to
    81	all exact executed members atomically; it performs no automatic follow-up.
    82	Phase 5 Step 3 may instead compose the transaction-bound execution and
    83	activation primitives under one outer transaction, leaving all exact
    84	experiments ``pending/train`` without starting scheduler work.
    85	Phase 5 Step 4 observes those exact members through one repeatable-read,
    86	read-only database snapshot and performs no lifecycle action.
    87	Phase 5 Steps 5a–5b compare each exact member's frozen recommendation evidence
    88	with its final result evidence without recomputation, persistence, or success
    89	policy. Step 5c then applies only a database-free versioned interpretation
    90	policy, keeping evidence sufficiency, campaign interpretation, operator-review
    91	eligibility, and the invariant absence of follow-up authority separate.
    92	Phase 6A validates exact Step 5A/5C canonical and direct identity alignment and
    93	builds a deterministic follow-up proposal only from an eligible favorable,
    94	explicitly non-authorizing decision. It does not recompute policy truth or add
    95	operator-review, persistence, activation, execution, or scheduler behavior.
    96	Detailed contracts remain in the Phase documents referenced in §12.
    97	
    98	## 3. Responsibilities
    99	
   100	### 3.1 Owned responsibilities
   101	
   102	Own deterministic proposal identity/generation, authoritative persistence and
   103	duplicate provenance, advisory score history, explicit review disposition, and
   104	their presentation.
   105	
   106	### 3.2 Dependencies
   107	
   108	Consumes completed experiment/final-analysis evidence from Volumes VI/VII.
   109	Only the explicit Phase 4C execution and activation primitives cross into
   110	experiment lifecycle; Phase 5 Steps 1–3 are confirmed orchestration callers
   111	of those existing primitives. Ranking, campaign planning, campaign review, and
   112	campaign approval have no downstream execution dependency. Outcome assessment
   113	and policy consume persisted evidence but have no lifecycle dependency or
   114	authority.
   115	The Phase 6A proposal consumes only their immutable typed values and has no
   116	database, CLI, service, repository, lifecycle, or scheduler dependency.
   117	
   118	### 3.3 Prohibited responsibilities
   119	
   120	Advisory evaluation, ranking, campaign planning, campaign review, and campaign
   121	approval MUST NOT create experiments, queue work, mutate experiment or
   122	scheduler state, infer reviewer identity, use
   123	score thresholds for authorization, or claim expected profitability. Phase 4C
   124	may create and activate exactly one experiment only through its separately
   125	invoked, audited manual commands.
   126	Phase 6A eligibility MUST NOT be treated as operator approval, follow-up
   127	authorization, campaign success, profitability evidence, persistence, or
   128	scheduler work.
   129	
   130	## 4. Architecture
   131	
   132	### 4.1 Components
   133	
   134	- Pure identity/policy and candidate-generation domain components.
   135	- Pure identity-bound Phase 6A follow-up-proposal domain component.
   136	- Pure manual conversion eligibility, source-consistency, and proposed-
   137	  specification domain component.
   138	- Repository-owned PostgreSQL mapping, scans, duplicates, scores, and reviews.
   139	- Append-only conversion-proposal persistence with exact canonical retries.
   140	- Services for explicit generation, scoring, evaluation, ranking/comparison,
   141	  inspection, and review use cases.
   142	- CLI parsing/validation/presentation outside scheduler polling.
   143	
   144	### 4.2 Control flow
   145	
   146	Completed evidence → deterministic source selection → pure candidates →
   147	collision-aware persistence → optional explicit score/evaluation/ranking. The
   148	Phase 4C proposal → review → paused execution → activation chain consists of
   149	separately invoked and audited manual actions. Phase 4D reads ranking and Phase
   150	4C history to plan and review; campaign approval records only an explicit human
   151	decision and adds no implicit arrow to mutation or execution.
   152	
   153	The governed campaign path is:
   154	
   155	```text
   156	recommendation ranking
   157	-> read-only campaign plan
   158	-> read-only campaign review
   159	-> explicit persisted campaign approval
   160	-> explicit approved-campaign materialization to Phase 4C proposals
   161	-> read-only exact campaign handoff
   162	-> explicit atomic Phase 4C proposal review for all exact campaign members
   163	-> either optional Phase 5 Step 1 execution then optional Step 2 activation
   164	-> or optional Phase 5 Step 3 atomic execution-and-activation launch
   165	-> existing scheduler lifecycle for ordinary pending experiments
   166	-> optional read-only Phase 5 Step 4 operational status snapshot
   167	-> optional read-only Step 5b outcome assessment
   168	-> optional pure Step 5c advisory policy interpretation
   169	-> optional pure Phase 6A follow-up proposal for later operator review
   170	```
   171	
   172	All displayed stages through exact proposal review are implemented through
   173	Phase 4D Step 6; Phase 4C execution and activation remain separately invoked
   174	actions. Phase 5 Step 1 invokes only the existing Phase 4C execution operation
   175	for the exact campaign membership. Phase 5 Step 2 separately invokes only the
   176	existing Phase 4C activation operation; neither step invokes the other.
   177	Phase 5 Step 3 is a separate command that reuses both transaction-bound
   178	authorities inside one transaction; it does not call either public command.
   179	Phase 5 Step 4 reads the immutable materialization and bounded downstream
   180	evidence only; it neither invokes Steps 1–3 nor contacts the scheduler process.
   181	Step 5b reuses that status lifecycle inside one read-only snapshot. Step 5c
   182	contains no repository or CLI and consumes only an already-built immutable
   183	assessment. Phase 6A consumes only the exact immutable assessment and policy
   184	decision and terminates at a non-authorizing proposal value.
   185	
   186	### 4.3 Ownership boundaries
   187	
   188	Canonical text decides identity; repository transactions decide persistence;
   189	pure scoring, planning, campaign-review, outcome-policy, and follow-up-proposal
   190	components decide advisory output; pure review rules decide legal transitions;
   191	and the operator separately
   192	supplies review, conversion, and activation actions. Only Phase 4C Steps 4–5
   193	may create or activate the one provenance-linked experiment. Campaign
   194	planning, review, approval, outcome assessment, outcome policy, and Phase 6A
   195	follow-up proposal never do.
   196	
   197	## 5. Data model
   198	
   199	### 5.1 Authoritative entities
   200	
   201	Recommendation policy, semantic/invocation configuration, recommendation scan,
   202	recommendation, score run/result/component, evaluation run/result/component,
   203	ranking snapshot/member, and review event.
   204	Conversion proposal, review decision, execution, activation, and campaign
   205	approval records are separate immutable audit entities; only their explicitly linked experiment is
   206	an experiment-lifecycle entity. Campaign plans and reviews are reconstructed,
   207	not persisted; Step 3 persists only their exact approved/rejected provenance.
   208	Campaign outcome assessments and policy decisions are point-in-time,
   209	non-persistent advisory values; their canonical identities bind exact upstream
   210	evidence but create no authoritative campaign decision.
   211	Phase 6A follow-up proposals are likewise non-persistent advisory values. Their
   212	canonical identities bind the exact assessment v2, policy v1, decision v1,
   213	campaign, materialization, ordered members, eligibility, and fixed
   214	non-authority semantics while excluding observation time.
   215	
   216	### 5.2 Provenance and versions
   217	
   218	Canonical text is authoritative; tagged hashes accelerate lookup. Persisted
   219	records retain source experiment/analysis/model, scan, policy, identity,
   220	structural mutation, source rank, score policy/components, and review snapshot.
   221	
   222	### 5.3 Invariants and legacy data
   223	
   224	Scan-associated rows require positive source rank and cannot detach from their
   225	originating scan. Proposed/approved identities remain active; rejected/expired
   226	matches remain historical blockers. Legacy NULL/NULL scan/rank rows are not
   227	backfilled and are excluded from operations requiring provenance.
   228	
   229	Review transitions are only proposed → approved, rejected, or expired. Review
   230	events are append-only to the runtime role. Approval is advisory and leaves
   231	`approved_experiment_id` null under Step 5.
   232	
   233	## 6. Transactions
   234	
   235	### 6.1 Read paths
   236	
   237	Evidence, list, detail, score history, evaluation history, ranking input, and
   238	review history use typed read-only repository paths. Ranking does not reopen
   239	source experiment metrics.
   240	
   241	### 6.2 Write paths
   242	
   243	Candidate persistence uses short collision-aware transactions. Score result and
   244	ordered components persist atomically. Evaluation results and their unchanged
   245	Step 4 components persist atomically without locking experiment evidence.
   246	Review locks one recommendation and updates status plus one immutable event in
   247	the same transaction. Ranking persists its complete member set atomically and
   248	then completes a ranking-owned snapshot after an exact count check.
   249	Conversion-proposal insertion locks only its accelerator-hash bucket, compares
   250	canonical text exactly under the bytewise ``C`` collation, and inserts one
   251	complete row in one transaction. The collision ordinal is storage metadata;
   252	canonical text alone remains authoritative.
   253	
   254	### 6.3 Failure semantics
   255	
   256	Invalid commands create no scan/event. Candidate failures are counted per scan.
   257	Score retries compare complete immutable results. Evaluation retains completed
   258	per-recommendation results if a later item fails, marks the run failed, and
   259	forbids adding new results to that terminal run; exact existing results remain
   260	verifiable. Review event failure rolls back status; terminal retries create no
   261	event. A ranking-member failure leaves no partial membership.
   262	
   263	## 7. Concurrency
   264	
   265	### 7.1 Conflict domain
   266	
   267	Generation conflicts on semantic configuration plus policy; scoring retries on
   268	score run plus recommendation; evaluation conflicts on canonical evaluation-run
   269	identity and evaluation run plus recommendation; ranking conflicts on canonical
   270	snapshot identity and snapshot plus evaluation result; review conflicts on one
   271	recommendation row.
   272	
   273	### 7.2 Locking and serialization
   274	
   275	Generation uses a transaction advisory key plus canonical rechecks and active
   276	uniqueness. Scoring uses uniqueness and complete retry comparison. Evaluation
   277	uses a short shared lock on its own run row while inserting an atomic result;
   278	it does not lock experiment evidence. Review uses `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` and
   279	one-event uniqueness. Ranking serializes identical member verification with a
   280	short `FOR UPDATE` lock on its ranking-owned snapshot. Unrelated snapshots and
   281	unrelated work remain concurrent.
   282	
   283	### 7.3 Winner, loser, and retry outcomes
   284	
   285	Concurrent identical generation returns one created/one existing result.
   286	Equivalent score retry reuses only an exact persisted result. Concurrent review
   287	produces one terminal winner and one `recommendation_review_status_conflict`;
   288	exactly one event exists. Concurrent identical ranking requests converge on one
   289	snapshot with an exactly verified member set.
   290	Concurrent identical conversion proposals converge on one exact canonical row;
   291	same-hash different canonical rows remain distinct.
   292	
   293	## 8. CLI
   294	
   295	### 8.1 Commands and validation
   296	
   297	Generation, scoring, evaluation, ranking/comparison, their inspection commands,
   298	review actions, and review inspection are explicit families. Evaluation,
   299	ranking, and review mutation
   300	are mutually exclusive with generation, scoring, scheduler, continuation, and
   301	experiment-lifecycle commands.
   302	
   303	### 8.2 Machine output
   304	
   305	`EXPERIMENT_RECOMMENDATION_*` records use stable fields, percent-escaped text,
   306	explicit `NULL`, deterministic ordering, and separate conflict/failure events.
   307	
   308	### 8.3 Human output
   309	
   310	Human score/evaluation/review summaries are concise, control-byte safe, and
   311	state that the result is advisory and created/queued no experiment. Ranking
   312	separates advisory-ready, blocked, and non-actionable presentation.
   313	
   314	## 9. Testing
   315	
   316	### 9.1 Pure tests
   317	
   318	Cover canonical identity/collisions, eligibility, candidates, scoring formulas,
   319	ranking, evaluation classification/identity, review parsing/reasons, and all
   320	transition outcomes. Phase 5 outcome tests additionally cover evidence
   321	classification, policy judgment, the advisory comparable-member evidence-
   322	coverage minimum, mixed member/metric states, locale independence,
   323	deterministic identity, and explicit non-authorization. The coverage minimum
   324	is not statistical sufficiency, confidence, causality, profitability,
   325	repeatability, or campaign success.
   326	Phase 6A pure tests additionally cover exact upstream alignment, stable refusal
   327	reasons, golden canonical identity, all non-authority flags, upstream-order,
   328	locale and observation-time invariance, identity sensitivity, inherited IEEE
   329	edge behavior, the canonical-size boundary, and inaccessible malformed
   330	construction paths.
   331	
   332	### 9.2 Persistence and migration tests
   333	
   334	Cover scans, duplicates, source rank/scan provenance, score ownership and
   335	immutability, review constraints, runtime privileges, SQLSTATEs, and migration
   336	repeatability. Evaluation tests additionally cover canonical idempotency,
   337	append-only result/component privileges, nullable blocked scores, and evidence
   338	foreign keys. Ranking tests cover exact membership, bucket/rank uniqueness,
   339	narrow privileges, scope/captured-membership trigger enforcement, bounded
   340	evidence loading, atomic member persistence, and Step 1 immutability.
   341	Conversion-proposal tests cover complete invocation round trips, exact retries,
   342	hash collisions, concurrent insertion, restrictive privileges, and unchanged
   343	experiment fixtures.
   344	
   345	### 9.3 Concurrency and integration tests
   346	
   347	Cover same-candidate generation, score retries, evaluation run/result retries
   348	and partial failures, review action races, unrelated reviews, rollback, exact
   349	cleanup, and before/after experiment/identity/score digests.
   350	
   351	### 9.4 Regression boundaries
   352	
   353	Steps 1–5 remain individually stable. Changes MUST NOT alter training,
   354	inference, continuation, experiment lifecycle, or scheduler behavior.
   355	
   356	## 10. Operational safety
   357	
   358	### 10.1 Runtime isolation
   359	
   360	No recommendation command enters scheduler polling. Integration uses disposable
   361	rows and exact cleanup without disturbing genuine experiments.
   362	
   363	### 10.2 Permissions and destructive operations
   364	
   365	Runtime access to review history and evaluation results/components is
   366	SELECT/INSERT only; evaluation-run updates are limited to lifecycle columns.
   367	Ranking members are append-only and ranking-snapshot updates are limited to
   368	lifecycle/count columns. Owner/test connections perform exact fixture cleanup.
   369	Conversion proposals grant runtime ``SELECT``/``INSERT`` access. Manual review
   370	decisions grant runtime ``SELECT`` plus column-limited ``INSERT`` for decision
   371	payload only; generated decision IDs and timestamps are not caller-writable.
   372	Their source-provenance foreign keys are restrictive. Review history is
   373	append-only, and the greatest generated decision ID yields the current
   374	pending/approved/rejected administrative disposition. This sequence-ID order is
   375	authoritative even when concurrent transactions commit in another order.
   376	Conversion activations likewise grant only ``SELECT`` and column-limited
   377	``INSERT`` plus sequence usage. Activation evidence is append-only; runtime
   378	``UPDATE``, ``DELETE``, and ``TRUNCATE`` are denied.
   379	Other immutable histories follow Volume I §7.3.
   380	
   381	### 10.3 Observability and recovery
   382	
   383	Scans/runs expose completion and counters; scores/events retain immutable
   384	provenance; explicit conflicts distinguish safe rejection from system failure.
   385	
   386	## 11. Future extensions
   387	
   388	### 11.1 Approved extension points
   389	
   390	Versioned policies, pure candidate/scoring components, typed repository/service
   391	APIs, and separate inspection commands.
   392	
   393	### 11.2 Deferred capabilities
   394	
   395	Experiment queueing/execution from conversion, multi-source attribution,
   396	automatic research campaigns, profitability evidence, and scheduler-managed
   397	recommendation work. Phase 4C Step 1 provides the pure proposed-
   398	specification contract, Step 2 provides durable proposal audit evidence, and
   399	Step 3 provides explicit append-only manual proposal review. Step 4 permits one
   400	explicit approved proposal to create one paused experiment. Step 5 permits a
   401	separate explicit operator action to make that exact experiment pending under
   402	the existing scheduler lifecycle.
   403	
   404	### 11.3 Required decisions
   405	
   406	ADR-0005 defines explicit conversion authorization, implementation identity,
   407	idempotent experiment creation, transactions, and audit history. Approval alone
   408	does not invoke conversion. Budgets, queueing, execution, and scheduler capacity
   409	remain deferred under ADR-0004.
   410	
   411	Phase 4C Step 2 adds the append-only
   412	``experiment_recommendation_conversion_proposal`` record and a narrow
   413	repository. Exact canonical text remains authoritative; same-hash distinct
   414	canonical identities receive separate collision ordinals, while concurrent
   415	identical inserts converge on one proposal. Optional ranking provenance is
   416	advisory, excluded from identity, and cannot authorize conversion. Runtime
   417	access is limited to ``SELECT``/``INSERT``; no scheduler path reads these rows.
   418	
   419	Phase 4C Step 3 adds explicit ``approve``/``reject`` decisions against an exact
   420	proposal primary key. A caller-visible request token makes CLI retries
   421	idempotent per proposal. New request tokens permit auditable reversals; the
   422	greatest decision ID defines the current disposition. Approval remains
   423	administrative evidence only and never creates or queues an experiment.
   424	
   425	Phase 4C Step 4 adds one explicit manual conversion transaction. It takes a
   426	proposal-specific transaction advisory lock, revalidates the immutable
   427	proposal, requires the latest serialized decision to be ``approve``, creates
   428	one ``paused`` experiment, and records immutable provenance linking the
   429	proposal, approving decision, and experiment. Unique proposal and experiment
   430	references make retries and concurrent requests converge. The scheduler does
   431	not poll conversion rows and a converted experiment is not queued or started.
   432	
   433	Phase 4C Step 5 adds one explicit activation transaction. It revalidates the
   434	Step 4 execution and exact created invocation, requires the experiment to
   435	remain in the pristine ``paused/train`` state, records immutable activation
   436	evidence, and changes only that experiment to ``pending/train``. The audit and
   437	lifecycle update are atomic. Exact retries return the same activation without
   438	reapplying the transition. The scheduler is unchanged and never reads the
   439	activation table; no worker is started by activation.
   440	
   441	Phase 4C Step 6 adds a read-only workflow aggregate over proposal, greatest-ID
   442	review disposition, exact execution authorization, activation evidence, and
   443	current experiment lifecycle. Stable states and deterministic diagnostics make
   444	healthy and inconsistent chains inspectable without adding schema, privileges,
   445	workflow mutation, scheduler polling, or worker behavior.
   446	
   447	Phase 4D Step 1 adds a pure, versioned campaign policy and a read-only aggregate
   448	over one explicit completed ranking snapshot, persisted recommendation source
   449	metrics, and the existing Phase 4C workflow derivation. Ranking global ordinal,
   450	recommendation ID, ranking member ID, then canonical evidence define the full
   451	presentation/selection order. Every considered
   452	candidate is retained with one decision and stable reasons; plan identity binds
   453	the full policy, scope, snapshot, evidence, workflow provenance, decisions, and
   454	reasons while excluding display time. There is no campaign table or scheduler
   455	consumer. Because no authoritative profitability evidence exists, a requested
   456	profitability threshold yields ``profitability_metric_unavailable`` rather than
   457	an inferred proxy.
   458	
   459	Phase 4D Step 2 adds a pure review contract over the Step 1 plan and reuses the
   460	same read-only loader and planner. It verifies plan identity, policy/scope,
   461	counts, result shape, and deterministic ordering; preserves selected and
   462	excluded rows with their ordered reasons; and derives exact canonical duplicate
   463	groups plus deterministic family, symbol, and horizon coverage. Review identity
   464	binds these results while excluding display time. Step 2 adds no migration,
   465	privilege, persisted campaign, workflow mutation, scheduler consumer, or worker
   466	behavior.
   467	
   468	Phase 4D Step 3 adds one immutable approval/rejection audit row for one exact
   469	Step 2 review. One PostgreSQL transaction loads the explicit ranking snapshot
   470	and Phase 4C workflow evidence, reconstructs and validates the plan and review,
   471	requires an operator-supplied expected review hash, and inserts the decision.
   472	Canonical review text is authoritative; identical retries converge, changed
   473	decision/reviewer/reason payload conflicts, and a zero-selection campaign may
   474	only be rejected. Runtime privileges are append-only and column-limited. The
   475	approval row never creates or modifies an experiment and is not consumed by
   476	the scheduler.
   477	
   478	Phase 4D Step 4 adds one explicit, atomic materialization transaction for one
   479	approved campaign. It reconstructs the exact plan, review, and approval, then
   480	passes every selected member through the existing Phase 4C conversion contract.
   481	One immutable manifest and ordered member links record created or reused Phase
   482	4C proposals. Canonical text is authoritative and exact replay converges;
   483	changed operator, reason, membership, proposal, or approval evidence conflicts.
   484	First creation reconstructs the approved evidence; retry validates the
   485	immutable manifest directly because its newly created proposals intentionally
   486	alter subsequent planning evidence.
   487	Materialization does not review or execute those proposals, create or modify an
   488	experiment, or contact the scheduler or workers.
   489	
   490	Phase 4D Step 5 adds a read-only campaign handoff projection. The immutable
   491	Step 4 manifest and ordered members remain membership authority; greatest-ID
   492	Phase 4C review, execution, activation, and experiment lifecycle evidence are
   493	observed in one repeatable-read transaction and one consistent snapshot.
   494	Explicit aggregate states and deterministic diagnostics expose incomplete or
   495	contradictory chains without persistence, repair, automatic progression,
   496	scheduler polling, or worker behavior.
   497	
   498	Phase 4D Step 6 adds one explicit atomic operator review over the exact stored
   499	Step 4 member order. It validates the existing Step 4 manifest and Step 5/Phase
   500	4C workflow evidence, serializes only the linked proposal review sequences, and
   501	appends one ordinary Phase 4C approve/reject row per member in one transaction.
   502	Deterministic request identity makes exact whole-campaign retries converge;
   503	opposite, unrelated same-decision, malformed, or partially satisfied evidence
   504	fails closed. No Phase 4D review authority or schema is added, and execution,
   505	activation, experiment creation, scheduling, workers, repair, and automatic
   506	progression remain separate.
   507	
   508	Phase 5 Step 1 adds one separately confirmed, all-member execution transaction
   509	over the same immutable Step 4 membership. Sorted existing Phase 4C proposal
   510	locks serialize the operation with direct review and direct execution. Every
   511	member is validated before the first insert, then the existing transaction-
   512	bound Phase 4C primitive creates ordinary paused experiments and immutable
   513	execution rows. Exact all-executed retry is already satisfied; mixed prior
   514	execution fails closed. There is no new schema or execution authority, and no
   515	activation, pending transition, scheduler action, worker launch, or automatic
   516	progression.
   517	
   518	Phase 5 Step 2 adds one separately confirmed, all-member activation transaction
   519	over that same membership. Existing activation advisory locks and experiment
   520	row locks are acquired in sorted execution-ID and experiment-ID order. All
   521	members are validated before the first ordinary activation insert and exact
   522	``paused/train`` to ``pending/train`` update. Exact fully activated retry is
   523	already satisfied only while every experiment retains that post-state; mixed
   524	activation fails closed. No schema, campaign activation authority, scheduler
   525	action, worker launch, direct process, or automatic follow-up is added.
   526	
   527	Phase 5 Step 3 adds one separately confirmed atomic launch over the same exact
   528	membership. It takes all proposal locks in ascending proposal-ID order,
   529	validates the complete execution phase, creates all required ordinary paused
   530	experiments and executions, then takes activation locks in ascending
   531	execution-ID order and experiment rows in ascending experiment-ID order. It
   532	validates the complete activation phase before applying any activation, and
   533	commits once. All-executed/no-activation state is completed atomically; partial
   534	execution or activation fails closed; an exact fully activated retry is
   535	already satisfied only while every experiment remains ``pending/train``. No
   536	schema, campaign lifecycle authority, scheduler action, worker launch, direct
   537	process, or automatic follow-up is added.
   538	
   539	Phase 5 Step 5a defines a pure immutable outcome assessment over exact campaign
   540	membership, lifecycle consistency, source/result provenance, comparison
   541	context, and metric deltas. Step 5b loads authoritative persisted campaign and
   542	scientific evidence in one repeatable-read, read-only snapshot and builds a
   543	deterministic, non-authoritative, point-in-time assessment from it. Neither step
   544	persists an assessment, declares campaign success, or authorizes follow-up.
   545	
   546	Phase 5 Step 5c adds a pure versioned policy over the Step 5a assessment. It
   547	uses the assessment's existing classifications and deltas, applies explicit
   548	metric-direction and advisory evidence-coverage rules, and separates evidence
   549	sufficiency, conservative interpretation, and eligibility for a later explicit
   550	operator review. Only a favorable, sufficient, all-comparable campaign is
   551	eligible for such review; neutral, unfavorable, mixed, and inconclusive
   552	campaigns are not. Its result is non-persistent and non-authoritative, always
   553	records follow-up authorization as false, and adds no repository, CLI,
   554	scheduler, worker, schema, or lifecycle behavior.
   555	
   556	Phase 6A adds the distinct
   557	``RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposal`` contract over one exact Step 5a
   558	assessment v2 and one exact Step 5c policy decision v1 containing policy v1.
   559	It validates authoritative canonical text as well as hashes and exact campaign,
   560	materialization, count, and ordered-member alignment. Only an eligible,
   561	favorable, explicitly non-authorizing decision yields a proposal. Contract v1
   562	binds every safety semantic and exact upstream canonical identity, excludes
   563	``observedAt``, and rejects canonical text above 1,048,576 bytes before
   564	construction. The proposal is not approval, persistence, activation,
   565	execution, scheduler work, success evidence, or authority for Phase 6B–6F.
   566

 ## 3. Responsibilities
 
 ### 3.1 Owned responsibilities

 ### 3.2 Dependencies

 ## 4. Architecture
 
 ### 4.1 Components
 
 - Pure identity/policy and candidate-generation domain components.
+- Pure identity-bound Phase 6A follow-up-proposal domain component.
 - Pure manual conversion eligibility, source-consistency, and proposed-
   specification domain component.
 - Repository-owned PostgreSQL mapping, scans, duplicates, scores, and reviews.
 - Append-only conversion-proposal persistence with exact canonical retries.
 - Services for explicit generation, scoring, evaluation, ranking/comparison,
   inspection, and review use cases.
 - CLI parsing/validation/presentation outside scheduler polling.
 
 ### 4.2 Control flow
 
 Completed evidence → deterministic source selection → pure candidates →
 collision-aware persistence → optional explicit score/evaluation/ranking. The
 Phase 4C proposal → review → paused execution → activation chain consists of
 separately invoked and audited manual actions. Phase 4D reads ranking and Phase
 4C history to plan and review; campaign approval records only an explicit human
 decision and adds no implicit arrow to mutation or execution.
 
 The governed campaign path is:
 
 ```text
 recommendation ranking
 -> read-only campaign plan
 -> read-only campaign review
 -> explicit persisted campaign approval
 -> explicit approved-campaign materialization to Phase 4C proposals
 -> read-only exact campaign handoff
 -> explicit atomic Phase 4C proposal review for all exact campaign members
 -> either optional Phase 5 Step 1 execution then optional Step 2 activation
 -> or optional Phase 5 Step 3 atomic execution-and-activation launch
 -> existing scheduler lifecycle for ordinary pending experiments
 -> optional read-only Phase 5 Step 4 operational status snapshot
 -> optional read-only Step 5b outcome assessment
 -> optional pure Step 5c advisory policy interpretation
+-> optional pure Phase 6A follow-up proposal for later operator review
 ```

 Phase 4D Step 6; Phase 4C execution and activation remain separately invoked

 for the exact campaign membership. Phase 5 Step 2 separately invokes only the
 existing Phase 4C activation operation; neither step invokes the other.
 Phase 5 Step 3 is a separate command that reuses both transaction-bound
 authorities inside one transaction; it does not call either public command.
 Phase 5 Step 4 reads the immutable materialization and bounded downstream

 ## 5. Data model
 
 ### 5.1 Authoritative entities
 
 Recommendation policy, semantic/invocation configuration, recommendation scan,
 recommendation, score run/result/component, evaluation run/result/component,
 ranking snapshot/member, and review event.
 Conversion proposal, review decision, execution, activation, and campaign
 approval records are separate immutable audit entities; only their explicitly linked experiment is
 an experiment-lifecycle entity. Campaign plans and reviews are reconstructed,
 not persisted; Step 3 persists only their exact approved/rejected provenance.
 Campaign outcome assessments and policy decisions are point-in-time,
 non-persistent advisory values; their canonical identities bind exact upstream
 evidence but create no authoritative campaign decision.
+Phase 6A follow-up proposals are likewise non-persistent advisory values. Their
+canonical identities bind the exact assessment v2, policy v1, decision v1,
+campaign, materialization, ordered members, eligibility, and fixed
+non-authority semantics while excluding observation time.
 
 ### 5.2 Provenance and versions
 
 Canonical text is authoritative; tagged hashes accelerate lookup. Persisted
 records retain source experiment/analysis/model, scan, policy, identity,
 structural mutation, source rank, score policy/components, and review snapshot.
 
 ### 5.3 Invariants and legacy data
 
 Scan-associated rows require positive source rank and cannot detach from their
 originating scan. Proposed/approved identities remain active; rejected/expired
 matches remain historical blockers. Legacy NULL/NULL scan/rank rows are not
 backfilled and are excluded from operations requiring provenance.
 
 Review transitions are only proposed → approved, rejected, or expired. Review
 events are append-only to the runtime role. Approval is advisory and leaves
 `approved_experiment_id` null under Step 5.
 
 ## 6. Transactions
 
 ### 6.1 Read paths
 
 Evidence, list, detail, score history, evaluation history, ranking input, and
 review history use typed read-only repository paths. Ranking does not reopen
 source experiment metrics.
 
 ### 6.2 Write paths
 
 Candidate persistence uses short collision-aware transactions. Score result and
 ordered components persist atomically. Evaluation results and their unchanged
 Step 4 components persist atomically without locking experiment evidence.
 Review locks one recommendation and updates status plus one immutable event in
 the same transaction. Ranking persists its complete member set atomically and
 then completes a ranking-owned snapshot after an exact count check.
 Conversion-proposal insertion locks only its accelerator-hash bucket, compares
 canonical text exactly under the bytewise ``C`` collation, and inserts one
 complete row in one transaction. The collision ordinal is storage metadata;
 canonical text alone remains authoritative.
 
 ### 6.3 Failure semantics
 
 Invalid commands create no scan/event. Candidate failures are counted per scan.
 Score retries compare complete immutable results. Evaluation retains completed
 per-recommendation results if a later item fails, marks the run failed, and
 forbids adding new results to that terminal run; exact existing results remain
 verifiable. Review event failure rolls back status; terminal retries create no
 event. A ranking-member failure leaves no partial membership.
 
 ## 7. Concurrency
 
 ### 7.1 Conflict domain
 
 Generation conflicts on semantic configuration plus policy; scoring retries on
 score run plus recommendation; evaluation conflicts on canonical evaluation-run
 identity and evaluation run plus recommendation; ranking conflicts on canonical
 snapshot identity and snapshot plus evaluation result; review conflicts on one
 recommendation row.
 
 ### 7.2 Locking and serialization
 
 Generation uses a transaction advisory key plus canonical rechecks and active
 uniqueness. Scoring uses uniqueness and complete retry comparison. Evaluation
 uses a short shared lock on its own run row while inserting an atomic result;
 it does not lock experiment evidence. Review uses `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` and
 one-event uniqueness. Ranking serializes identical member verification with a
 short `FOR UPDATE` lock on its ranking-owned snapshot. Unrelated snapshots and
 unrelated work remain concurrent.
 
 ### 7.3 Winner, loser, and retry outcomes
 
 Concurrent identical generation returns one created/one existing result.
 Equivalent score retry reuses only an exact persisted result. Concurrent review
 produces one terminal winner and one `recommendation_review_status_conflict`;
 exactly one event exists. Concurrent identical ranking requests converge on one
 snapshot with an exactly verified member set.
 Concurrent identical conversion proposals converge on one exact canonical row;
 same-hash different canonical rows remain distinct.
 
 ## 8. CLI
 
 ### 8.1 Commands and validation
 
 Generation, scoring, evaluation, ranking/comparison, their inspection commands,
 review actions, and review inspection are explicit families. Evaluation,
 ranking, and review mutation
 are mutually exclusive with generation, scoring, scheduler, continuation, and
 experiment-lifecycle commands.
 
 ### 8.2 Machine output
 
 `EXPERIMENT_RECOMMENDATION_*` records use stable fields, percent-escaped text,
 explicit `NULL`, deterministic ordering, and separate conflict/failure events.
 
 ### 8.3 Human output
 
 Human score/evaluation/review summaries are concise, control-byte safe, and
 state that the result is advisory and created/queued no experiment. Ranking
 separates advisory-ready, blocked, and non-actionable presentation.
 
 ## 9. Testing
 
 ### 9.1 Pure tests
 
 Cover canonical identity/collisions, eligibility, candidates, scoring formulas,
 ranking, evaluation classification/identity, review parsing/reasons, and all
 transition outcomes. Phase 5 outcome tests additionally cover evidence
 classification, policy judgment, the advisory comparable-member evidence-
 coverage minimum, mixed member/metric states, locale independence,
 deterministic identity, and explicit non-authorization. The coverage minimum
 is not statistical sufficiency, confidence, causality, profitability,
 repeatability, or campaign success.
+Phase 6A pure tests additionally cover exact upstream alignment, stable refusal
+reasons, golden canonical identity, all non-authority flags, upstream-order,
+locale and observation-time invariance, identity sensitivity, inherited IEEE
+edge behavior, the canonical-size boundary, and inaccessible malformed
+construction paths.
 
 ### 9.2 Persistence and migration tests
 
 Cover scans, duplicates, source rank/scan provenance, score ownership and
 immutability, review constraints, runtime privileges, SQLSTATEs, and migration
 repeatability. Evaluation tests additionally cover canonical idempotency,
 append-only result/component privileges, nullable blocked scores, and evidence
 foreign keys. Ranking tests cover exact membership, bucket/rank uniqueness,
 narrow privileges, scope/captured-membership trigger enforcement, bounded
 evidence loading, atomic member persistence, and Step 1 immutability.
 Conversion-proposal tests cover complete invocation round trips, exact retries,
 hash collisions, concurrent insertion, restrictive privileges, and unchanged
 experiment fixtures.
 
 ### 9.3 Concurrency and integration tests
 
 Cover same-candidate generation, score retries, evaluation run/result retries
 and partial failures, review action races, unrelated reviews, rollback, exact
 cleanup, and before/after experiment/identity/score digests.
 
 ### 9.4 Regression boundaries
 
 Steps 1–5 remain individually stable. Changes MUST NOT alter training,
 inference, continuation, experiment lifecycle, or scheduler behavior.
 
 ## 10. Operational safety
 
 ### 10.1 Runtime isolation
 
 No recommendation command enters scheduler polling. Integration uses disposable
 rows and exact cleanup without disturbing genuine experiments.
 
 ### 10.2 Permissions and destructive operations
 
 Runtime access to review history and evaluation results/components is
 SELECT/INSERT only; evaluation-run updates are limited to lifecycle columns.
 Ranking members are append-only and ranking-snapshot updates are limited to
 lifecycle/count columns. Owner/test connections perform exact fixture cleanup.
 Conversion proposals grant runtime ``SELECT``/``INSERT`` access. Manual review
 decisions grant runtime ``SELECT`` plus column-limited ``INSERT`` for decision
 payload only; generated decision IDs and timestamps are not caller-writable.
 Their source-provenance foreign keys are restrictive. Review history is
 append-only, and the greatest generated decision ID yields the current
 pending/approved/rejected administrative disposition. This sequence-ID order is
 authoritative even when concurrent transactions commit in another order.
 Conversion activations likewise grant only ``SELECT`` and column-limited
 ``INSERT`` plus sequence usage. Activation evidence is append-only; runtime
 ``UPDATE``, ``DELETE``, and ``TRUNCATE`` are denied.
 Other immutable histories follow Volume I §7.3.
 
 ### 10.3 Observability and recovery
 
 Scans/runs expose completion and counters; scores/events retain immutable
 provenance; explicit conflicts distinguish safe rejection from system failure.
 
 ## 11. Future extensions
 
 ### 11.1 Approved extension points
 
 Versioned policies, pure candidate/scoring components, typed repository/service
 APIs, and separate inspection commands.
 
 ### 11.2 Deferred capabilities
 
 Experiment queueing/execution from conversion, multi-source attribution,
 automatic research campaigns, profitability evidence, and scheduler-managed
 recommendation work. Phase 4C Step 1 provides the pure proposed-
 specification contract, Step 2 provides durable proposal audit evidence, and
 Step 3 provides explicit append-only manual proposal review. Step 4 permits one
 explicit approved proposal to create one paused experiment. Step 5 permits a
 separate explicit operator action to make that exact experiment pending under
 the existing scheduler lifecycle.
 
 ### 11.3 Required decisions
 
 ADR-0005 defines explicit conversion authorization, implementation identity,
 idempotent experiment creation, transactions, and audit history. Approval alone
 does not invoke conversion. Budgets, queueing, execution, and scheduler capacity
 remain deferred under ADR-0004.

     1	Phase 5 Recommendation Campaign Outcome Assessment
     2	==================================================
     3	
     4	Purpose and boundary
     5	--------------------
     6	
     7	Step 5a defines a pure, immutable, point-in-time domain assessment of the
     8	scientific outcomes associated with an exact recommendation-campaign
     9	materialization.  It is read-only, non-persistent, non-authoritative, and does
    10	not declare campaign success or authorize follow-up work.
    11	
    12	Lifecycle, consistency, and comparison
    13	--------------------------------------
    14	
    15	Lifecycle is explicit (``not_terminal``, ``succeeded``, ``failed``,
    16	``cancelled``, or ``unknown``).  Consistency is independent
    17	(``consistent`` or ``inconsistent``), and inconsistent downstream evidence is
    18	retained with deterministic diagnostic codes.  Callers can also carry a known
    19	inconsistent lifecycle or workflow observation without changing or discarding
    20	the exact materialized-member identity.  Scientific comparisons are derived
    21	only for consistent succeeded members.  Member outcomes distinguish not-ready,
    22	comparable success, context-changed success, metric-gap success, terminal
    23	failure, terminal cancellation, and inconsistency.
    24	
    25	Multi-metric evidence
    26	---------------------
    27	
    28	Source and result evidence contain metric collections.  Collections reject a
    29	duplicate metric identity and are canonicalized by metric identity, so input
    30	order does not affect output or assessment identity.  A comparison is derived
    31	for every metric identity in the source/result union.  Member outcome counts
    32	remain separate from metric-comparison and delta counts.
    33	
    34	Provenance and deterministic identity
    35	-------------------------------------
    36	
    37	Each materialized member may identify its expected downstream experiment.
    38	Succeeded-result evidence is checked against that exact experiment.  Terminal
    39	members require an expected experiment, and expected experiments, observed
    40	result experiments, result models, and typed result identities may not be
    41	reused across members.  Unexpected result evidence is retained and diagnosed
    42	rather than discarded.  Provenance defects remain inconsistent members when
    43	top-level materialization membership is trustworthy; invalid or ambiguous
    44	member identity fails the assessment.  Campaign and materialization inputs
    45	must agree on both the persisted campaign-approval ID and its canonical
    46	identity hash.
    47	
    48	Canonical text and hashing bind lifecycle, consistency, diagnostics, canonical
    49	source and result metrics, comparisons, exact provenance, and aggregate member
    50	and metric summaries.  Authoritative campaign and materialization canonical
    51	texts are length-framed into the assessment identity alongside their compact
    52	hashes.  Canonical number formatting is locale-independent.  ``observed_at``
    53	is intentionally excluded from evidence identity.
    54	
    55	Non-goals
    56	---------
    57	
    58	Step 5a does not provide a repository, database access, persistence, service,
    59	CLI, scheduler, worker, filesystem behavior, campaign-success policy, or
    60	follow-up authorization.
    61	
    62	Step 5b authoritative-evidence integration
    63	------------------------------------------
    64	
    65	Step 5b supplies the read-only integration without changing the Step 5a domain
    66	boundary.  One PostgreSQL ``REPEATABLE READ``, ``READ ONLY`` transaction loads
    67	authoritative persisted evidence: the exact materialization through the Phase
    68	4D production loader, its exact campaign approval, and the evidence underlying
    69	lifecycle and workflow consistency from the existing Phase 5 campaign-status
    70	projection.  Step 5b builds a non-authoritative, point-in-time assessment from
    71	that evidence.  It does not reconstruct a second lifecycle classifier.
    72	
    73	The Step 5a campaign identity is the persisted approval canonical text and
    74	hash.  Its materialization input receives the materialization row's persisted
    75	``approval_identity_hash`` unchanged, so Step 5a verifies the approval-to-
    76	materialization binding.  Exact materialization member ordinal, member ID,
    77	ranking-member ID, recommendation ID, source-experiment ID, proposal ID, and
    78	the execution-linked expected experiment ID flow from the validated status
    79	snapshot.  A status member reported as inconsistent is passed to Step 5a as
    80	``inputConsistency=inconsistent``; Step 5b neither repairs nor normalizes the
    81	upstream evidence.
    82	
    83	Scientific evidence
    84	-------------------
    85	
    86	Source evidence follows the materialized recommendation's persisted source
    87	experiment, model, and analysis identities.  Source final-inference selection
    88	uses the immutable source invocation canonical text captured by the exact
    89	persisted Phase 4C proposal; it never substitutes the source experiment's
    90	current configuration.  Result evidence follows the exact conversion-
    91	execution experiment, its current linked model, and its final inference and
    92	final analysis rows.  The comparison context is taken from the selected
    93	persisted final inference identity: canonical symbol, prediction horizon,
    94	threshold, persisted window size, the versioned
    95	``inference_eval_result_label_v1`` representation of the
    96	``label_rule_id``/``target_type`` pair, and canonical ``YYYY-MM-DD`` inference
    97	range.
    98	
    99	The version-1 Step 5b mapping carries ``inference_accuracy`` and
   100	``leader_score`` with ``NumericDelta`` support.  The source values are the
   101	immutable values captured on the recommendation; result values are the final
   102	analysis values.  Missing analysis or metric evidence remains absent or null,
   103	and changed contexts remain non-comparable.  No metric is recomputed and no
   104	campaign-success threshold is applied.
   105	
   106	Other persisted analysis fields were deliberately not mapped in this version:
   107	the immutable recommendation does not retain a directly corresponding value
   108	with the same scientific meaning.  In particular, Step 5b does not reconstruct
   109	predicted-neutral proportions or evidence totals from result counts.  Such
   110	values therefore cannot be mistaken for a valid numeric delta.
   111	
   112	CLI and output
   113	--------------
   114	
   115	::
   116	
   117	   LSTM_Release \
   118	     --recommendation-campaign-outcome-assessment=MATERIALIZATION_ID
   119	
   120	The separated option form is also accepted.  The command is intrinsically
   121	read-only, so ``--yes`` and ``--dry-run`` are rejected.  Output begins with one
   122	``RECOMMENDATION_CAMPAIGN_OUTCOME_ASSESSMENT`` record and then one
   123	``RECOMMENDATION_CAMPAIGN_OUTCOME_ASSESSMENT_MEMBER`` record per exact
   124	materialized ordinal.  Records expose contract and identity hashes, the exact
   125	Step 5a aggregate classification and counts, lifecycle, separate input and
   126	final consistency, diagnostics, provenance, contexts, metrics, comparisons,
   127	explicit evidence/context-presence booleans and ``null`` values,
   128	percent-encoded variable text, the materialization's persisted campaign-
   129	approval hash, and explicit no-write/no-scheduler/no-success/no-follow-up
   130	safety fields.
   131	
   132	No schema migration or privilege change is required.  The assessment remains
   133	point-in-time and non-persistent; Step 5b inserts, updates, deletes, activates,
   134	queues, retries, and launches nothing and authorizes no follow-up.
   135	
   136	Step 5c pure outcome policy
   137	----------------------------
   138	
   139	Step 5c adds only a database-free policy and interpretation contract over one
   140	immutable Step 5a assessment.  It does not reopen source or result evidence,
   141	recompute a metric or delta, or change any Step 5a lifecycle, consistency,
   142	member-outcome, comparison, diagnostic, or aggregate classification.  Evidence
   143	classification and policy judgment remain separate fields.
   144	
   145	Policy contract version 1 has an explicit canonical identity.  Its default
   146	minimum comparable-member evidence coverage is one ``succeeded_comparable``
   147	member, and its required metric rules are ``inference_accuracy`` and
   148	``leader_score``, each with the explicit ``higher_is_favorable`` direction.
   149	Required rules are sorted by metric identity and duplicates are rejected.  A
   150	caller may construct another version-1 policy with a different positive
   151	minimum or deterministic set of metric-direction rules; changing the policy
   152	changes both policy and decision identity.  The canonical policy binds the
   153	contract version, coverage minimum, sorted metric identities and directions,
   154	fixed all-member consistency, terminal, and successful comparability
   155	requirements, favorable-interpretation requirement for operator-review
   156	eligibility, and fixed non-authorizing semantics.
   157	
   158	``minimumComparableMemberCount`` is only an advisory evidence-coverage
   159	threshold.  It is not statistical significance, confidence, causal evidence,
   160	profitability evidence, a guarantee of repeatability, or campaign success.  No
   161	materiality threshold or statistical, causal, profitability, or weighted
   162	campaign score is inferred.
   163	
   164	For every exact member and required metric, the policy output preserves the
   165	Step 5a comparison classification and delta as optional evidence, then records
   166	a separate ``favorable``, ``neutral``, ``unfavorable``, or ``not_evaluable``
   167	judgment.  It never subtracts result and source values again.  Positive and
   168	negative meaning is determined only by the versioned metric-direction rule;
   169	an exact zero remains neutral.
   170	
   171	Evidence sufficiency is separate from campaign interpretation.  Inconsistent,
   172	not-ready, cancelled, context-changed, metric-gap, missing-source,
   173	missing-result, unavailable, unsupported, missing-required-metric, and
   174	minimum-comparable-member conditions remain explicit conservative reasons.
   175	A terminal failure is adverse lifecycle evidence rather than a scientific
   176	metric gap.  Thus an all-failed campaign is interpreted ``unfavorable`` even
   177	though it lacks the minimum comparable-member evidence coverage; a failed
   178	member mixed with complete favorable evidence is ``mixed``.  Cancellation,
   179	inconsistency, unfinished lifecycle, or non-comparable successful evidence
   180	makes the campaign interpretation ``inconclusive``.  Complete comparable
   181	metric judgments yield ``favorable``, ``neutral``, ``unfavorable``, or
   182	``mixed`` without declaring the campaign successful.
   183	
   184	Follow-up eligibility is only ``eligible_for_operator_review`` when every
   185	exact member is a comparable successful outcome, the minimum evidence coverage
   186	is met, all required metrics are comparable, and the campaign interpretation
   187	is ``favorable``.  Neutral, unfavorable, mixed, and inconclusive campaigns are
   188	``not_eligible``; sufficient evidence alone is not enough.  Failure,
   189	cancellation, incompleteness, inconsistency, context change, or a metric gap
   190	also leaves it ``not_eligible``.  This is an advisory screening result, not a
   191	recommendation, approval, or authorization: the immutable result always has
   192	``follow_up_authorized=false`` and ``follow_up_authorizing=false``.
   193	
   194	Decision contract version 1 binds the complete policy canonical text and hash,
   195	the exact Step 5a assessment canonical text and hash, complete campaign
   196	approval and materialization identities, ordered member identities including
   197	the expected experiment, assessment lifecycle/consistency/outcome/diagnostics,
   198	evidence classifications, metric judgments, interpretations, reasons, counts,
   199	and explicit non-authorization result.  The complete upstream assessment
   200	canonical already binds Step 5a provenance; the direct fields are deliberately
   201	included as well because the decision carries and exposes those identities and
   202	assessment classifications.  ``observed_at`` remains display metadata and is
   203	excluded through the upstream assessment identity.  Unsupported policy or
   204	assessment contracts, invalid enums, duplicate policy metrics, duplicate or
   205	ambiguous top-level member identities, malformed identity/hash pairs, and
   206	invalid counts fail closed.
   207	
   208	Step 5c adds no repository, service, formatter, CLI, migration, privilege,
   209	table, sequence, lock, write, scheduler call, worker behavior, experiment or
   210	campaign mutation, persistence, operator-review event, follow-up generation,
   211	approval, queueing, activation, retry, continuation, or automatic action.  The
   212	existing Step 5b CLI continues to report only the non-authoritative assessment
   213	built from authoritative persisted evidence and does not silently apply outcome
   214	policy.
     1	Phase 5 Step 4 — Recommendation Campaign Operational Status
     2	=============================================================
     3	
     4	Purpose and authority
     5	---------------------
     6	
     7	Phase 5 Step 4 is a read-only point-in-time projection for one persisted Phase
     8	4D campaign materialization. It reports every exact member's ordinary Phase 4C
     9	review, execution, activation, experiment lifecycle, worker metadata, model,
    10	final inference, and final analysis evidence. It creates no campaign status or
    11	lifecycle authority and persists nothing.
    12	
    13	The immutable ordered rows in
    14	``experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member`` are the only
    15	membership source. The production Phase 4D loader validates the manifest,
    16	canonical identity and hash, selected count, contiguous ordinals, unique links,
    17	and exact proposal provenance before downstream status is projected.
    18	
    19	Snapshot and query contract
    20	---------------------------
    21	
    22	One PostgreSQL ``REPEATABLE READ``, ``READ ONLY`` transaction owns the complete
    23	snapshot. The operation takes no advisory or row locks, performs no write or
    24	sequence call, and uses bounded exact-ID queries for the materialized proposals
    25	and their linked experiments. Unrelated workflow and experiment rows cannot
    26	become campaign members.
    27	
    28	``observed_at`` is one PostgreSQL transaction timestamp shared by every output
    29	row. It is metadata, not identity. The deterministic version-1 snapshot
    30	identity binds the validated materialization and every ordered member's durable
    31	review, execution, activation, experiment lifecycle, worker, model, phase-
    32	completion, exact completed/failed final-result counts, consistency, and
    33	diagnostic projection.
    34	Persisted lifecycle timestamps are evidence and are bound; ``observed_at`` and
    35	local wall-clock time are not identity inputs. The identity contains no random
    36	value, local command process ID, transaction ID, or unordered iteration. A
    37	persisted ``worker_pid`` is bound as database evidence but is not treated as a
    38	live-process observation.
    39	
    40	Member and aggregate status
    41	---------------------------
    42	
    43	Execution, activation, operational state, terminal result, and consistency are
    44	separate dimensions. Operational states distinguish proposal-only, executed
    45	paused, pending scheduler claim, running train/infer/analyze, completed, failed,
    46	cancelled, paused after progress, and inconsistent evidence. An execution keeps
    47	its immutable original authorizing approval even when the greatest current
    48	review-decision ID later records rejection.
    49	
    50	Final inference is configured only when both persisted inference dates exist.
    51	For ordinary recommendation-conversion experiments, the existing scheduler
    52	requires that range after training and advances completed final inference to
    53	final analysis. Successful ``completed/done`` therefore requires the exact
    54	final inference row selected by the scheduler (current model, symbol, horizon,
    55	threshold, and dates) and completed final analysis for the current model. A
    56	persisted ``completed/done`` recommendation-conversion experiment without that
    57	configured pipeline is reported as inconsistent rather than treated as a
    58	train-only success.
    59	
    60	Unknown lifecycle values, invalid cardinality or provenance, activation without
    61	execution, missing experiments, incompatible activation/lifecycle state,
    62	incoherent worker evidence, and missing configured terminal results remain
    63	visible as deterministic member diagnostics. A valid materialization still
    64	returns every ordered member when downstream evidence is malformed. An invalid
    65	materialization rejects the command because exact membership cannot be trusted.
    66	Any inconsistent member forces aggregate ``inconsistent`` status.
    67

    88	The snapshot is advisory and may become stale immediately after its transaction

    94	
    95	No migration or privilege change is required. Runtime access uses existing

#pragma once

#include <optional>
#include <set>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace EA::ExperimentRecommendation
{

inline constexpr const char* kCoreLrMult = "core_lr_mult";
inline constexpr const char* kHeadLrMult = "head_lr_mult";
inline constexpr const char* kLabelThreshold = "label_threshold";
inline constexpr const char* kPredictionHorizon = "prediction_horizon";

enum class RecommendationSourceScope
{
    symbolHorizon,
    symbol,
    global
};

enum class RecommendationStatus
{
    proposed,
    rejected,
    expired,
    approved
};

enum class RecommendationDuplicateType
{
    noDuplicate,
    existingExperiment,
    activeRecommendation,
    excludedTerminalExperiment
};

struct RecommendationPolicy
{
    bool enabled = true;
    double minimumLeaderScore = 0.0;
    double minimumInferenceAccuracy = 0.0;
    std::optional<double> maximumPredictedNeutralProportion = 0.80;
    int topSourcesPerScope = 3;
    int maximumRecommendationsPerSource = 4;
    int maximumRecommendationsPerScan = 20;
    int minimumEvidenceCount = 1;
    std::set<std::string> allowedParameters{
        kCoreLrMult, kHeadLrMult, kLabelThreshold};
    std::vector<double> coreLrOffsets{-0.25, 0.25};
    std::vector<double> headLrOffsets{-0.5, 0.5};
    std::vector<double> labelThresholdOffsets{-0.0001, 0.0001};
    bool allowHorizonChanges = false;
    std::vector<int> permittedHorizons;
    RecommendationSourceScope sourceScope =
        RecommendationSourceScope::symbolHorizon;
    bool terminalExperimentsAreDuplicates = true;
    std::optional<int> expirationDays;
    int policyVersion = 1;
};

// These are the experiment-row fields that define the reproducible research
// question supported by Phase 4A. Runtime state, orchestration policy, lineage,
// and provenance are deliberately excluded. The schema audit in the Phase 4A
// foundation document records persisted model settings that cannot yet be
// round-tripped through an experiment row; Phase 4A must not guess them.
struct EffectiveExperimentConfiguration
{
    std::string symbol;
    int predictionHorizon = 0;
    double labelThreshold = 0.0;
    std::optional<double> coreLrMult;
    std::optional<double> headLrMult;
    int targetEpochs = 0;
    std::string trainStartDate;
    std::string trainEndDate;
    std::optional<std::string> inferStartDate;
    std::optional<std::string> inferEndDate;
};

// Invocation identity is deliberately distinct from semantic configuration
// identity. A resume model supplies initial weights and optimizer progress, so
// it materially distinguishes executions without changing the hyperparameter
// and data-selection question represented above. Checkpoint cadence controls
// persistence/evaluation opportunities rather than ordinary training math.
struct ExperimentInvocationConfiguration
{
    EffectiveExperimentConfiguration configuration;
    int checkpointInterval = 20;
    std::optional<long long> resumeModelId;
};

struct RecommendationSource
{
    long long experimentId = -1;
    std::optional<long long> modelId;
    std::optional<long long> analysisId;
    ExperimentInvocationConfiguration invocation;
    std::optional<double> leaderScore;
    std::optional<double> inferenceAccuracy;
    std::optional<double> predictedNeutralProportion;
    long long evidenceCount = 0;
};

struct RecommendationCandidateIdentity
{
    EffectiveExperimentConfiguration configuration;
    std::string canonicalText;
    std::string hash;
};

struct RecommendationInvocationIdentity
{
    ExperimentInvocationConfiguration invocation;
    std::string canonicalText;
    std::string hash;
};

RecommendationCampaignStatusMemberInput StatusMember(
    int ordinal,
    RecommendationCampaignStatusTerminalResult terminal =
        RecommendationCampaignStatusTerminalResult::succeeded,
    std::optional<long long> experimentId = std::nullopt)
{
    RecommendationCampaignStatusMemberInput member;
    member.memberOrdinal = ordinal;
    member.materializationMemberId = 100 + ordinal;
    member.rankingMemberId = 200 + ordinal;
    member.recommendationId = 300 + ordinal;
    member.sourceExperimentId = 400 + ordinal;
    member.proposalId = 500 + ordinal;
    member.currentReviewDecisionId = 600 + ordinal;
    member.currentReviewDecision = "approve";
    if (terminal == RecommendationCampaignStatusTerminalResult::notTerminal)
        return member;

    member.authorizationReviewDecisionId = 600 + ordinal;
    member.executionId = 700 + ordinal;
    member.activationId = 800 + ordinal;
    member.experimentId = experimentId.value_or(900 + ordinal);
    member.executionCount = 1;
    member.activationCount = 1;
    RecommendationCampaignStatusExperimentEvidence experiment;
    experiment.experimentId = *member.experimentId;
    experiment.symbol = "eurusd";
    experiment.predictionHorizon = 12;
    experiment.targetEpochs = 120;
    experiment.invocationMode = "recommendation_conversion";
    experiment.invocationIdentityCanonical = "integration-invocation";
    experiment.invocationProvenanceValid = true;
    if (terminal == RecommendationCampaignStatusTerminalResult::succeeded)
    {
        experiment.status = "completed";
        experiment.phase = "done";
        experiment.completedAt = "2026-07-19 12:00:00+00";
        experiment.modelId = 1000 + ordinal;
        experiment.modelLinkCount = 1;
        experiment.inferStartPresent = true;
        experiment.inferEndPresent = true;
        experiment.inferConfigured = true;
        experiment.inferenceResultCount = 1;
        experiment.completedInferenceResultCount = 1;
        experiment.analysisResultCount = 1;
        experiment.completedAnalysisResultCount = 1;
    }
    else if (terminal == RecommendationCampaignStatusTerminalResult::failed)
    {
        experiment.status = "failed";
        experiment.phase = "train";
        experiment.completedAt = "2026-07-19 12:00:00+00";
        experiment.errorMessage = "worker_failed";
    }
    else if (terminal == RecommendationCampaignStatusTerminalResult::cancelled)
    {
        experiment.status = "cancelled";
        experiment.phase = "train";
        experiment.completedAt = "2026-07-19 12:00:00+00";
    }
    else
    {
        experiment.status = "malformed";
        experiment.phase = "unknown";
    }
    member.experiment = std::move(experiment);
    return member;
}

RecommendationCampaignStatusSnapshot StatusSnapshot(
    std::vector<RecommendationCampaignStatusMemberInput> members)
{
    RecommendationCampaignStatusInput input;
    input.materializationId = 71;
    input.materializationContractVersion =
        kRecommendationCampaignMaterializationContractVersion;
    input.materializationIdentityCanonical =
        "integration-materialization-canonical";
    input.materializationIdentityHash = RecommendationCanonicalHash(
        input.materializationIdentityCanonical);
    input.selectedMemberCount = static_cast<int>(members.size());
    input.observedAt = "2026-07-19 12:00:00+00";
    input.members = std::move(members);
    return BuildRecommendationCampaignStatusSnapshot({71}, std::move(input));
}

RecommendationCampaignPlanningPolicy Policy()
{
    RecommendationCampaignPlanningPolicy value;
    value.enabled = true;
    value.maximumPerSourceExperiment.reset();
    return value;
}

class StreamStateGuard
{
public:
    explicit StreamStateGuard(std::ostream& stream)
        : stream_(stream), flags_(stream.flags()),
          precision_(stream.precision()), locale_(stream.getloc()) {}

    ~StreamStateGuard()
    {
        try
        {
            stream_.flags(flags_);
            stream_.precision(precision_);
            stream_.imbue(locale_);
        }
        catch (...)
        {
        }
    }

private:
    std::ostream& stream_;
    const std::ios_base::fmtflags flags_;
    const std::streamsize precision_;
    const std::locale locale_;
};

template <typename Value>
void PrintOptional(std::ostream& output, const std::optional<Value>& value)
{
    if (value) output << *value;
    else output << "null";
}

void PrintOptionalNumber(
    std::ostream& output,
    const std::optional<double>& value)
{
    if (value) output << CanonicalRecommendationDouble(*value);
    else output << "null";
}

void PrintSafety(std::ostream& output)
{
    output << "transaction_read_only=true,snapshot_isolation=repeatable_read,"
              "advisory_locks_acquired=0,row_locks_acquired=0,rows_inserted=0,"
              "rows_updated=0,rows_deleted=0,sequences_advanced=0,"
              "scheduler_started=false,scheduler_signaled=false,"
              "scheduler_polled=false,workers_launched=false,"
              "automatic_follow_up=false,campaign_state_row_created=false,"
              "assessment_persisted=false,assessment_advisory=true,"
              "campaign_success_declared=false,follow_up_authorized=false";
}

Consistency InputConsistency(
    const RecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentMember& member)
{
    return std::find(member.diagnostics.begin(), member.diagnostics.end(),
               RecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentDiagnosticCode::
                   InputEvidenceInconsistent) == member.diagnostics.end()
        ? Consistency::Consistent
        : Consistency::Inconsistent;
}

void PrintDiagnostics(
    std::ostream& output,
    const std::vector<
        RecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentDiagnosticCode>& diagnostics)
{
    if (diagnostics.empty())
    {
        output << "none";
        return;
    }
    for (std::size_t index = 0; index < diagnostics.size(); ++index)
    {
        if (index != 0) output << '|';
        output << RecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentDiagnosticCodeText(
            diagnostics[index]);
    }
}

void PrintContext(
    std::ostream& output,
    const Context* context,
    const char* prefix)
{
    output << ',' << prefix << "_symbol=";
    if (context) output << RecommendationMachineText(context->symbol);
    else output << "null";
    output << ',' << prefix << "_prediction_horizon=";
    if (context) output << context->predictionHorizon;
    else output << "null";
    output << ',' << prefix << "_threshold=";
    if (context) output << CanonicalRecommendationDouble(context->threshold);
    else output << "null";
    output << ',' << prefix << "_window_size=";
    if (context) output << context->windowSize;
    else output << "null";
    output << ',' << prefix << "_label_definition=";
    if (context)
        output << RecommendationMachineText(context->labelDefinition);
    else output << "null";
    output << ',' << prefix << "_inference_range_start=";
    if (context)
        output << RecommendationMachineText(context->inferenceRangeStart);
    else output << "null";
    output << ',' << prefix << "_inference_range_end=";
    if (context)
        output << RecommendationMachineText(context->inferenceRangeEnd);
    else output << "null";
}

std::optional<double> MetricValue(
    const MetricCollection* collection,
    const std::string& identity)
{
    if (!collection) return std::nullopt;
    const auto found = std::find_if(collection->metrics.begin(),
        collection->metrics.end(), [&](const auto& metric)
    {
        return metric.identity == identity;
    });
    return found == collection->metrics.end()
        ? std::nullopt
        : found->value;
}

void PrintMetrics(
    std::ostream& output,
    const MetricCollection* metrics)
{
    if (!metrics || metrics->metrics.empty())
    {
        output << "none";
        return;
    }
    for (std::size_t index = 0; index < metrics->metrics.size(); ++index)
    {
        const auto& metric = metrics->metrics[index];
        if (index != 0) output << '|';
        output << RecommendationMachineText(metric.identity) << ':';
        PrintOptionalNumber(output, metric.value);
        output << ':'
               << RecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentMetricComparisonSupportText(
                      metric.comparisonSupport);
    }
}

void PrintResultIdentities(
    std::ostream& output,
    const std::vector<
        RecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentResultIdentity>* identities)
{
    if (!identities || identities->empty())
    {
        output << "none";
        return;
    }
    for (std::size_t index = 0; index < identities->size(); ++index)
    {
        if (index != 0) output << '|';
        output << RecommendationMachineText((*identities)[index].kind)
               << ':' << (*identities)[index].id;
    }
}

void PrintComparisons(
    std::ostream& output,
    const std::vector<
        RecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentMetricComparison>& comparisons)
{
    if (comparisons.empty())
    {
        output << "none";
        return;
    }
    for (std::size_t index = 0; index < comparisons.size(); ++index)
    {
        const auto& comparison = comparisons[index];
        if (index != 0) output << '|';
        output << RecommendationMachineText(comparison.metricIdentity) << ':'
               << RecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentMetricComparisonClassificationText(
                      comparison.classification)
               << ':';
        PrintOptionalNumber(output, comparison.sourceValue);
        output << ':';
        PrintOptionalNumber(output, comparison.resultValue);
        output << ':';
        PrintOptionalNumber(output, comparison.delta);
        output << ':';
        if (comparison.contextDifferences.empty()) output << "none";
        else
        {
            for (std::size_t difference = 0;
                 difference < comparison.contextDifferences.size();
                 ++difference)
            {
                if (difference != 0) output << '+';
                output << RecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentContextDifferenceText(
                    comparison.contextDifferences[difference]);
            }
        }
    }
}
